text:
The judge should instruct the jury that self-defense requires a reasonable belief in imminent unlawful force, and the father’s mistaken belief—though honest—must be tested for reasonableness given the son’s history of violence and the kicking down of the door. If the jury finds the belief objectively reasonable under those circumstances, self-defense applies despite the son’s actual lack of intent to harm; if not, it does not.
CONFIDENCE: 85
